item.title: Licensing Captain Post
item.content:encoded: It's a problem. We will not allow its use. If you post it to the site, we will delete it. Period.

item.title: Re: Realistic Portal gun SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
I was claiming the story laid out in the the Central narrative section of my idea as my own. I am plaining on fully acknowledging the 'Portal' aspect of the article and using that as a base, similar to many other articles on this site based on Minecraft or 'Where's Wally'.

That said, if the Portal aspect of the article causes commons issues I will drop the idea. What is the policy on using licensed properties as inspiration for an article?

item.title: Re: Realistic Portal gun SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
I had no intention of claiming the concept of Portal guns as my own.

By posting content to the SCP wiki, which is licensed under creative commons, you are claiming the material you write is your own. Your concept states "The anomaly is a stereotypical portal gun, that looks entirely like one from the game 'Portal' and functions as such." This would not be compliant with creative commons.

item.title: Re: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded: Sorry, I did not think I was over the limit. I have shortened it.

item.title: Re: Realistic Portal gun SCP idea
item.content:encoded: By Creative Common I meant the policy for in-game images. I had no intention of claiming the concept of Portal guns as my own. Sorry for the miscommunication.

item.title: Re: Realistic Portal gun SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Hi, Licensing Staff here. Don't.

Taking a well-known object, one that you specifically mention was directly taken from the Portal franchise, and adding little twists to it is not enough to turn it into its own intellectual property.

If you're using someone's IP to the point where you're unsure of where it falls in line with Creative Commons, the safe answer is always to just let it be and do something else.

item.title: Realistic Portal gun SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, description, experimentation and recovery log

Elevator Pitch: There are many 'Portal' type anomalies in the SCP foundation, but never one that functions as a Gun. But what would happen if one existed.

Central Narrative: The anomaly is a stereotypical portal gun, that looks entirely like one from the game 'Portal' and functions as such. However, there are two twists to this concept:

+ Twists
- Close

1. Whenever someone makes a logical deduction about how a device would work, based on various aspects of science such as anti-matter or wormholes, the device will conform to that conclusion. For example, if a foundation scientist deduced that the edges of the portal would logically be superheated and produce large amounts of plasma, the portals will start doing so. The only exceptions to this are conclusions that would pre-empt the existence of the device or its initial functionality of shooting portals. These effects halt when the portal gun is deactivated. Eventually the foundation gets the bright idea to use the gun to create a generator, manned by uneducated D-Class, which ends in disaster when one realizes the portals violate the conservation of energy.

2. The device was recovered from a Level 2 reality bender. However this reality bender was also a quantum physicist and had built up an unshakable belief in the science, leading to the self-suppression of his abilities when they emerged. However the reality bender (hereafter called 'Bob') was also a fan of science fiction, especially the game 'Portal'. 'Bob' attended a sci-fi con with a model portal gun he had built himself and was discussion the possibility of making a real one in the future via use of quantum physics. Some of the other people at the con made fun of this, making him angry and temporarily un-suppressing his reality bending. Bob caused his portal to become 'real' and shot an actual portal, before realizing how such a thing wasn't possible. This lead to the anomaly in its current state. Bob was severely injured by the resulting extreme temperatures before the device was shut down by undercover agents at the sci-fi con. In hospital Bob writes a note about the clash between fiction and reality leading to his downfall before dying.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A concept that would usually be placed in a -J article being presented seriously.

Additional Notes: I am unsure of the Creative Commons policy for game icons.
